# Designing a serial protocol: framing, checksums, CRC: the exercise

<!-- Generated by tools/maintainer/build_exercise_readmes.py from the lesson page. Edit the lesson, then run the script. -->

Lesson: [Designing a serial protocol: framing, checksums, CRC](https://jouhis.github.io/embedded-course/lessons/0103-designing-a-serial-protocol.html). Read it first: the steps below refer to its diagrams and worked examples.

## Try it on the Pico: a framed sensor stream

The Pico project is `projects/0103-framed-sensor-stream`. Each frame carries a sequence number, a sensor ID, a 16-bit reading and a CRC, all COBS-encoded and ended by a zero. The body is six bytes: one sequence byte, one sensor ID byte (0x21), the reading as two bytes, and the two CRC bytes. The reading is a temperature in hundredths of a degree, starting at 22.50 C.

1. Open `projects/0103-framed-sensor-stream/starter` in VS Code. The starter's `frame_encode()` returns 0, so the serial monitor shows five lines like `FRAME seq=0 bytes=0:` with no bytes after them, then `ROUNDTRIP FAILED`.
2. In `main.c`, fill in `frame_encode()`, following the comment: body, CRC, COBS, then the delimiter. Then fill in `frame_decode()`: COBS-decode, check the body length, check that the CRC of all six bytes is zero, and read the fields back.
3. Build with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd>, then start the simulator with <kbd>F1</kbd> → *Wokwi: Start Simulator*. You will know it works when each of the five `FRAME` lines is followed by bytes, and the last line is `ROUNDTRIP OK`.

The starter's `main()` checks only that all five frames decode. The reference solution in `projects/0103-framed-sensor-stream/solution` adds two things you may want to copy after you have your own version working: a `decoded seq=... value=...` line for each frame, and a check that a frame with one byte flipped is rejected, which prints `corrupted frame rejected: yes` before the final line. The solution's output ends with `ROUNDTRIP OK`.

We did not run the simulator for this lesson, because the workspace has no `WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN`. The reference solution's logic was run on the PC: it compiles against the same COBS and CRC files, and its output ends with `ROUNDTRIP OK`. The Wokwi run is the step to confirm.
